finding.claim: Missing authorization enforcement in wipe(): requireRole() only returns a boolean and never throws, but wipe() discards the result, so any caller can wipe any tenant regardless of role.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (or any caller supplying a User object) invoking POST /tenants/{t}/wipe with an arbitrary tenant id, without the OWNER role.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, which destroys the tenant's data.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. Both parameters come from the caller.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called as a bare statement and its boolean return value is ignored.
requireRole is documented as 'Returns true if the user holds the role. Does not throw', so a missing role produces no exception.

finding.guards_checked: checkRole (lines 18-22) throws SecurityException, but wipe() does not call it. export() at line 32 correctly uses checkRole, which shows the intended behavior. No other check on the path: no tenant-ownership check and no caller-side filter, since the file has no other code. The require* name suggests it throws, which makes the mistake easy to miss.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (Admin.java:14) returns boolean and never throws; its result is discarded at line 26. checkRole (18-22) throws but is only used in export(). No other guard.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:26 calls requireRole as a bare statement, discarding its boolean (defined at :14-16, non-throwing), so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any user without the OWNER role.
